motif.variation: statement on lead-thin (p1) - Vxx-repainted with Sxx chokes (p2/p3) - displaced +2 rows with per-row duty automation inside a sustained note (p4) - chopped to three-note fragments in the break (p9) - all three duties cycling (p11) - displaced +4 rows (p12)

qa.notes: FRACTIONAL SWING is the groove: tempo 160 / speed 6 gives 5.625 ticks per row, so rows alternate 6 6 5 6 6 5 6 5 by design and evenTempo is false. The riff is written on off-beats - attacks at rows 3, 6, 10, 13 of each bar rather than 0, 4, 8, 12 - so the alternation is maximally audible; cite the statement at 2:0 -> 2:60. TRESILLO (9.1 recipe C, 8th-level 6+6+4, which is the grouping the doc prescribes at 140-160 BPM): the triangle bass attacks at rows 0, 6, 12 of every 16-row bar right through the A sections and A'', cited 2:0 -> 2:60 and 14:0 -> 16:60, against a kit that stays on the beat above it. POLYMETER (recipe D): in B the riff moves to pulse 2 and is RE-GROUPED onto a 6-row dotted-quarter cell whose phase is carried across the whole section - entry rows 0/2/4/0 at frames 8/9/10/11 (64-row frames: entry = (-64k) mod 6), cited 8:0 -> 11:60. Same pitches, new grid; 2 against 3 with the half-time kit. HEMIOLA (recipe E): the last three bars of the piece accent every 6 rows - 17:16, 17:22, 17:28, 17:34, 17:40, 17:46, 17:52, 17:58 - eight groups closing exactly on the barline, carried by kit, triangle and both pulses at once. METRIC SURPRISE (recipe H): D param 0 at 13:59 ends the break a beat early so A'' returns displaced; the render is 1148 rows, not 1152. DISPLACEMENT (recipe F): the riff is restated +2 rows at 6:2 and +4 rows at 15:4, both well over the +-2 the doc requires at this tempo. COUNTERPOINT: pulse 2 is an independent line, never a doubling - in A its nine attacks (2:8, 2:12, 2:20, 2:24, 2:28, 2:36, 2:40, 2:52, 2:56) all land on rows the riff leaves empty, and in A'' it runs a descending counter-line ABOVE the riff, the piece's one deliberate voice crossing, at 14:4 -> 14:60. WRITTEN DISSONANCES, two. (1) A PREPARED SUSPENSION at the Bb7 -> Eb change inside B: pulse 1 attacks a flat 5 (80) at 9:56 as the seventh of the Bb7 bar, holds it across the change to Eb at 10:0 where it is the fourth, and resolves down by step to g5 (79) at 10:4, Eb's third - the frame-10 downbeat carries no pulse-1 attack precisely so the suspension can sound. The same figure returns in A'': pulse 2 attacks a flat 4 at 14:52 over the bVI, holds it through the change to G7 at 14:54 where it is the flat ninth, and resolves down by step to g4 at 14:56 (frame 15 shares the pattern; frame 16 states it a row later at 16:53 -> 16:57). (2) The cadential one is 11:0, where the augmented sixth's f sharp 5 is attacked over an a flat bass and resolves OUTWARD - f sharp up to g5 at 11:32 while the triangle falls a flat to g. HARMONY, three distinct non-diatonic devices in three sections: (1) augmented sixth at 11:0 - triangle a flat 2 (the flat 6), pulse 2 the tonic c, pulse 1 the sharp 4 f sharp 5 - resolving outward to G7 at 11:32, which is also where the piece's blue tritone becomes structural rather than decorative; (2) chromatic bass descent c - b natural - b flat - a flat, one link per half-bar, 12:0 -> 12:48, over a held c pedal in pulse 2 so the harmony is implied by the collision, arriving on a g dominant pedal at 13:0; (3) chained secondary dominants D7 -> G7 -> Cm at 17:0 -> 17:34, voiced with 0 param 74 (04a = dominant seventh, no fifth) on pulse 2 so the f sharp and b natural are both audible. The blue flat 5 (g flat 4 = 66) is a passing tone on a weak position in every statement of the riff - 2:13, resolving up to g4 at 2:14 - a wink, not a wound. Harmonic rhythm differs per section: A moves two bars of Cm then one bar each of Fm and G7, B moves one chord per two bars, and the break holds one chord per half-bar under the chromatic walk. NO STOCK LOOP (9.3): the A backbone is not a four-chord cycle left to run - every phrase is broken before the cycle can reach eight bars, and the break is a different chord each time. Frames 2/3: the last beat of bar 2 is a SECONDARY DOMINANT, C7 = V/iv, with the bass on c at 2:28 and pulse 2 spelling it with 0 param 74 at 2:28 (returned to the minor triad at 2:36), resolving into Fm at 2:32. Frames 4/5: bar 4 opens on the bVI, A flat, at 4:48 and falls a semitone to G7 at 4:54. Frames 6/7 (A'): bar 4 opens on the bIII, E flat, at 6:50 before G7 at 6:56. Frames 14/15/16 (A''): the bVI again at 14:48 falling to G7 at 14:54, which is where the second written suspension lives. Longest unbroken run of the four-chord cycle anywhere in the piece: five bars. DUTY AUTOMATION IS THE HOOK, and the engine fact that makes it work: Vxx is INERT against any instrument carrying a duty macro, because the macro overwrites the duty register on the next tick. So the two instruments that carry the hook - x-switch-cutter-blade (vol-lead) and x-switch-cutter-edge (vol-pluck) - deliberately have NO duty macro, which is what lets Vxx own their timbre per row. A repaints every two bars (V01/V02/V00/V02 at 2:0, 2:16, 2:32, 2:48); frames 3 and 5 are the same notes with a different V sequence, so the ONLY thing that changes between those repeats is timbre; A' automates duty INSIDE one sustained note, V00/V01/V02/V01/V00/V02/V01/V00 every two rows at 6:34 -> 6:48; A'' cycles all three duties every eight rows. The third x- instrument, x-switch-cutter-buzz, carries dut-pwm-fast for the +4-displaced restatement at 15:4, where the shimmer replaces the Vxx repaints entirely. Sxx staccato chokes make the riff spit: S param 2 cuts a 5-or-6 tick row after two ticks, S param 3 in frames 3 and 5, and the whole break is choked (12:0 onward). DECIMAL PARAMS: 0 param 55 = 037 minor triad, 0 param 71 = 047 major triad, 0 param 74 = 04a dominant seventh, 0 param 0 = cancel, V param 0/1/2 = 12.5/25/50 percent duty, A param 15 = A0f, a fast swell UP into the return (13:48, cancelled with A param 0 at 13:58 before the frame is cut short), D param 0 = enter the next frame at row 0, B param 2 = loop to frame 2. The piece's global peak is b flat 5 = 82 at 17:58, the last of the hemiola's eight accents, reached by a rising broken-chord close eb4-g4-b flat 4-eb5-b flat 5 across 17:34 -> 17:58 with both pulses in unison - the last third of the form, on the accent that closes exactly on the barline. The suite-wide rmsRange convention: the measured two-pass mix RMS +-1.5 dB, declared per song because the design's [-20,-9] window is unreachable on this engine and the floor is -30 dBFS. Measured -22.67 dBFS, declared [-24.17, -21.17].
